I would like to have / need something like the following lift:

def Quotient.liftFun {X : Sort w} {α : Sort u} {s : Setoid α} {β : Sort v}
     (g : (X → α) → β)
     (h : ∀ f₁ f₂ : X → α, (∀ x, f₁ x ≈ f₂ x) → g f₁ = g f₂)
   : (X → Quotient s) → β := sorry

But that seems to not be possible with using the axiom of choice or unsafe and I'm wondering why. I tried to get the clanker (Opus 5.5) to explain it to me but I don't really get it, it should be as sound and computable as the Quotient.lift functions. If I have a computable function X → Quotient s and am able to prove about another (g) that it's invariant over a closure that produces the base type as long as it is equal to the Quotient.

For context I'm trying to define Monad.bind on a Quotient type of mine (trying to implement Interaction Trees in Lean4) but to do that I have the bind continuation A → ITree E B (where ITree is the quotient type) which I somehow need to "pierce" to access the actual underlying base type so I can make a resulting bound ITree.

Dealing with Quotient types is a bit new to me but I don't understand why you can practically erase them with Quotient.lift but there doesn't seem to be a way to do the same if you're given one under a function?

(In case you want the full context of what this is for: https://gist.github.com/Philogy/3d716c34825483d275e89049ddef61f3, check out bind in FullITree.lean, that's what I'm stuck defining, disclosure: the lean4 in the gist was written with the help of LLMs)

But that seems to not be possible with using the axiom of choice or unsafe and I'm wondering why

Did you mean "without using the axiom of choice or unsafe"?

Weiyi Wang said:

But that seems to not be possible with using the axiom of choice or unsafe and I'm wondering why

Did you mean "without using the axiom of choice or unsafe"?

You can easily define it noncomputably using the axiom of choice:

noncomputable def Quotient.liftFun
  {X : Sort w} {α : Sort u} {s : Setoid α} {β : Sort v}
  (g : (X → α) → β) -- note that the noncomputable version doesn't even need the hypothesis that `g` behaves the same over all base values which feels wrong to me
  (q : X → Quotient s) : β
  := g (fun x => Classical.choose (Quot.exists_rep (q x)))

You could then make it computable using unsafe:

private unsafe def Quotient.liftFunImpl g q := g (fun x => unsafeCast (q x))

@[implemented_by Quotient.liftFunImpl]
def Quotient.liftFun ... :=

What happens if you put the equivalence relation on X -> alpha defined by f equivalent to g iff for all x, f x equivalent g x, and then attempt to write down an equivalence between the quotient and X -> Quotient s?
I've wondered myself but this is unsafe, i.e. you can use it to prove False under native_decide; see #Is there code for X? > Lifting a quotient function @ 💬

You can even use it to decide arbitrary propositions!
(modified from version posted at #mathlib4 > computing quotient choice @ 💬)

import Mathlib.Data.Setoid.Basic

-- suppose this were computable by implementing it as `sorry`
def Quotient.liftFun {X : Sort w} {α : Sort u} {s : Setoid α} {β : Sort v}
     (g : (X → α) → β)
     (h : ∀ f₁ f₂ : X → α, (∀ x, f₁ x ≈ f₂ x) → g f₁ = g f₂)
   : (X → Quotient s) → β := sorry

-- and suppose it behaves nicely
theorem Quotient.liftFun_apply
    {X : Sort w} {α : Sort u} {s : Setoid α} {β : Sort v}
    (g : (X → α) → β)
    (h : ∀ f₁ f₂ : X → α, (∀ x, f₁ x ≈ f₂ x) → g f₁ = g f₂)
    (f : X → α) : Quotient.liftFun g h (fun x => Quotient.mk s (f x)) = g f := sorry

-- we derive a quotient version of the axiom of choice
def Trunc.choice {ι : Type*} {α : ι → Type*}
    (f : (i : ι) → Trunc (α i)) : Trunc ((i : ι) → α i) :=
  -- we follow the proof of `Quotient.pliftOn`
  let s : Setoid (Sigma α) := Setoid.comap Sigma.fst ⊥
  let lf (i : ι) : Quotient s :=
    Trunc.lift (fun x => Quotient.mk s ⟨i, x⟩)
      (fun _ _ => Quotient.sound rfl) (f i)
  have hgf1 (g : ι → Sigma α) (i : ι) :
      Quotient.mk s (g i) = lf i ↔ (g i).fst = i :=
    @Trunc.ind (α i) (fun x : Trunc (α i) =>
        Quotient.mk s (g i) =
          Trunc.lift (fun x => Quotient.mk s ⟨i, x⟩)
            (fun _ _ => Quotient.sound rfl) x ↔
        (g i).fst = i) (fun _ => Quotient.eq) (f i)
  (@Quotient.liftFun ι (Sigma α) s
      ((c : ι → Quotient s) × (c = lf → Trunc ((i : ι) → α i)))
      (fun g => ⟨fun i => Quotient.mk s (g i), fun h =>
        Trunc.mk fun i => Eq.rec (motive := fun x _ => α x) (g i).snd ((hgf1 g i).mp (congrFun h i))⟩)
      (fun f₁ f₂ hff =>
        have feq : (fun i => Quotient.mk s (f₁ i)) = (fun i => Quotient.mk s (f₂ i)) :=
          funext fun i => Quotient.sound (hff i)
        Sigma.ext feq (Subsingleton.helim
          (congrArg (fun c => c = lf → Trunc ((i : ι) → α i)) feq) _ _)) lf).snd <|
    -- we use the axiom of choice here
    -- but it's only inside a proof so this doesn't impact computability
    have hlf : (fun i => Quotient.mk s
        ⟨i, Classical.choice (@Trunc.ind (α i) (fun _ => Nonempty (α i)) Nonempty.intro (f i))⟩) = lf :=
      funext fun i => (hgf1 (fun i =>
        ⟨i, Classical.choice (@Trunc.ind (α i) (fun _ => Nonempty (α i)) Nonempty.intro (f i))⟩) i).mpr rfl
    Eq.rec (motive := fun x _ => Sigma.fst (Quotient.liftFun _ _ x) = x)
      (congrArg Sigma.fst (Quotient.liftFun_apply _ _ _)) hlf

def propDecidable (p : Prop) : Decidable p :=
  -- we follow the proof of `Classical.em`
  let S : Setoid Bool :=
    { r x y := x = y ∨ p
      iseqv :=
        { refl _ := .inl rfl
          symm h := h.imp_left Eq.symm
          trans h₁ h₂ := h₂.elim (· ▸ h₁) Or.inr } }
  have f (i : Quotient S) : Trunc { x : Bool // Quotient.mk S x = i } :=
    i.recOnSubsingleton fun x => Trunc.mk ⟨x, rfl⟩
  (Trunc.choice f).recOnSubsingleton fun g =>
    let u : Bool := (g (Quotient.mk S true)).1
    let v : Bool := (g (Quotient.mk S false)).1
    have u_def : u = true ∨ p := Quotient.exact (g (Quotient.mk S true)).2
    have v_def : v = false ∨ p := Quotient.exact (g (Quotient.mk S false)).2
    have not_uv_or_p : u ≠ v ∨ p :=
      match u_def, v_def with
      | Or.inr h, _ => Or.inr h
      | _, Or.inr h => Or.inr h
      | Or.inl hut, Or.inl hvf =>
        have hne : u ≠ v := by simp [hvf, hut]
        Or.inl hne
    have p_implies_uv (hp : p) : u = v :=
      congrArg (fun i => (g i).1) (Quotient.sound (Or.inr hp))
    decidable_of_iff (u = v) ⟨not_uv_or_p.neg_resolve_left, p_implies_uv⟩
